takeaways: Sensitivity labels fail on rollout design, not tooling: keep four or five plain-language labels that describe handling rules rather than departments, and test them against real documents.

Let the system do most of the classifying with defaults, light recommendations and auto-labeling run in simulation first, and reserve encryption for the top tier after testing a client compatibility matrix.
Copilot surfaces whatever users can already reach, so fix oversharing first, label the highest-risk stores, pilot with a clean group and measure coverage, correctness and protected content.
hook: Many sensitivity label rollouts look green on the dashboard while protecting almost nothing. This episode is for information protection owners, Purview admins and compliance teams who want a practical path from pilot to production, covering taxonomy, encryption, defaults, auto-labeling, container labels and Copilot readiness.
